name: Adenocarcinoma of the Gallbladder and Extrahepatic Biliary Tract

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Histopathological and Radiological Diagnostic Criteria for Gallbladder and Extrahepatic Biliary Tract Adenocarcinoma

criteria.description: Histological confirmation of adenocarcinoma in gallbladder or extrahepatic bile duct tissue
Imaging evidence (CT, MRI, or ultrasound) of mass lesion or biliary obstruction in gallbladder or extrahepatic bile ducts
Clinical symptoms consistent with biliary tract malignancy such as jaundice or right upper quadrant mass
Elevated serum CA 19-9 or CEA levels supportive but not diagnostic

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation plus imaging evidence of tumor in gallbladder or extrahepatic bile ducts
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires exclusion of metastatic adenocarcinoma from other primary sites.

pathognomonic.notes: Indicative of bile duct obstruction by tumor
Mass arising from gallbladder or bile duct
searchTerms: lump felt in right upper belly

common.symptomName: Abdominal pain localized to right upper quadrant

searchTerms: skin itching due to liver problems

occasional.notes: May indicate secondary infection or tumor necrosis
Due to biliary obstruction or tumor effect
Due to tumor extension or liver metastasis

rare.notes: May occur in advanced disease with peritoneal involvement
Secondary to hypoalbuminemia or lymphatic obstruction

laboratory: Increased alkaline phosphatase and gamma-glutamyl transferase
Elevated tumor markers CA 19-9 and carcinoembryonic antigen (CEA)
imaging: Ultrasound showing gallbladder mass or bile duct dilation
CT or MRI demonstrating mass lesion in gallbladder or extrahepatic bile ducts
genetic: No specific germline mutations identified; somatic mutations in KRAS, TP53, and ERBB2 reported
other: Endoscopic retrograde cholangiopancreatography (ERCP) for biopsy and biliary stenting

distinguishingFeatures: Tumor located within intrahepatic bile ducts
May present with different clinical symptoms

redFlags: Unexplained weight loss with biliary obstruction
references: Bridgewater J, Galle PR, Khan SA, et al. Guidelines for the diagnosis and management of cholangiocarcinoma: an update. Gut. 2014;63(8):1389-1402.
Razumilava N, Gores GJ. Cholangiocarcinoma. Lancet. 2014;383(9935):2168-2179.
